source_review.notes: Reviewed the current C++ allocator draft, Python memory/getsizeof/tracemalloc documentation, Rust Layout documentation, jemalloc manual, Google Benchmark guide, Valgrind Massif manual, current Open Data Structures Python edition, and CLRS fourth-edition publisher record. Nine final destinations returned HTTP 200; MIT Press returned an automated access-control response while the edition and bibliographic identity were independently checked.

evidence: Checked trace totals, allocation counts/bytes, peak-live maximum, prefix accounting, potential telescoping, asymptotic quantifiers, expectations, and space decomposition.
Checked that worst-case, average-case, expected, amortized, and high-probability quantities have distinct definitions and assumptions.
Checked size parameters, output sensitivity, ownership scope, and allocation lifetime terminology.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Wall-clock and physical-memory measurements are explicitly outside the mathematical primitive-count model.

evidence: Recomputed capacities 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 and cumulative copies 0, 1, 3, 7, 15 for the modeled targets.
Recomputed allocation counts 0 through 5 and transient peak slots 0, 1, 3, 6, 12, 24.
Checked the exact-power and between-power cases for ceil(log2(n))+1 allocations and copies 2^k-1 below 2n.
numerical_recomputation.notes: All counts are abstract slot/write/allocation events rather than runtime byte measurements.

evidence: Derived the geometric copy sum 1+2+...+2^(k-1)=2^k-1.
Re-derived aggregate and accounting proofs for stack multipop and the potential telescoping condition.
Verified symbolic array/list space formulas keep headers, pointers, padding, slack, and allocator rounding parameterized.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: No platform constants are invented or generalized across runtimes.

evidence: Reviewed n=0/1, exact powers, just-after-growth sizes, maximum capacity, integer overflow, allocation failure, old/new buffer coexistence, shrink thrashing, and deamortization.
Reviewed variable-length keys, collision adversaries, adaptive inputs, tails versus means, shallow/shared objects, GC, pools, arenas, fragmentation, retained memory, RSS, and virtual memory.
Reviewed setup contamination, timer resolution, optimization, warm/cold state, drift, correlation, instrumentation scope, and flight-control hard-budget boundaries.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Hard latency and memory guarantees are not inferred from amortized or empirical averages.

evidence: Every cost claim must bind operation, parameters, valid-state family, workload/quantifier, model, guarantee type, and assumptions.
Payload, metadata, slack, auxiliary, transient, retained, resident, virtual, and cumulative-allocation measures remain separate.
Every amortized accounting prefix remains nonnegative and physical measurements are tied to implementation/toolchain/environment identity.
invariant_checking.notes: Multidimensional feasibility constraints are preserved instead of collapsed into an arbitrary score.

evidence: Reviewed the doubling-array copy proof line by line across capacity intervals and exact-power boundaries.
Reviewed stack multipop credits: one stored credit per resident element, no element removed twice, and nonnegative balance for every prefix.
Reviewed potential-method preconditions, initial potential, lower bound, per-case change, and telescope.
proof_review.notes: The chapter presents mathematical proof structures, not machine-checked proofs of any allocator or runtime.

evidence: Cost-model, space-accounting, and measurement-correspondence sections state their assumptions and limitations.
The flight-controller example enumerates real-time, systems, safety, security, quality, domain, and regulatory review and claims none.
Legacy fixed benchmark prescriptions were not repeated as universal scientific requirements.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No measurement, asymptotic theorem, or local model is represented as deployment assurance.

evidence: The extracted Python model completed with zero exit status, exact seven-line stdout, and empty stderr.
The model explicitly emits evidence=modeled_counts_not_memory_measurement.
Nine references were directly retrieved, the MIT access-control limit recorded, and the stale Open Data Structures URL replaced before digest binding.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No wall-clock benchmark, heap profiler, allocator statistic, hardware counter, or real-time system was executed.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed cost models, asymptotic quantifiers, amortization, growth factors, space layers, allocation events/lifetimes, fragmentation, failure, workloads, measurement design, statistics, and instrumentation boundaries.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed claim-scaled benchmark design, reproducibility identity, transient peaks, allocator/GC scope, capacity arithmetic, adversarial inputs, fault injection, raw results, and contract-relevant tails.

pedagogical_review.notes: Builds directly on DSE-001 through DSE-003, distinguishes proof from measurement, uses an exact executable cost model, counters fourteen misconceptions, supplies ten worked examples, and closes with five matched exercises and answers.

limitations: Internal authoring, source, mathematical, snippet, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external algorithms, allocator, runtime, systems, security, real-time, flight-control, safety, regulatory, quality, or independent validation review is claimed. The chapter and finite model prove neither arbitrary implementation complexity, physical memory usage, allocator behavior, timing bounds, real-time safety, certification, nor deployment fitness.
